chapter_theme: Two songs at Rameswaram (இராமேசுரம்): a whole life from youth's trade and pleasures among price-women to old age with a stick and a list of diseases, and the endless sweetness of unions that hides the Lord's feet; the praise tells of Brahma beaten for not knowing Om and of Rama's deeds.

983.reading: The poet runs through a life: youth, beauty, play, trade, a worthless life thought to last a hundred years, building mansions and seeking wealth, perfumes and flowers, and whirling for some days in desire for price-women; then wrinkled skin, grey hair, blindness, faltering legs, deafness, a stick, and colic, itch, phlegm, wind, diabetes, anaemia, scrofula, fever and cough, until the body stinks like filth, and he asks whether he must perish so. The praise tells how Murugan struck the four-faced Brahma who could not explain the ground of Om, beating his four heads, names him son of the goddess and bridegroom of the hunter girl of knowledge, and lists Rama's deeds against Tataka, Subahu, the seven trees, Vali, Viradha, the sea and Ravana before ending at Rameswaram where the Vedas are chanted.
983.nuance: The song is a life in two quatrains, built on chains of -ஆகி and -மாறி (ஆகி ... ஆகி, then மாறி ... மாறி), so that each stage becomes the next and each faculty changes away. ஓம் என அதாரம் உரையாத பிரமாவை விழ மோதி பொருள் ஓதுக என: the Om myth is explicit. பசு பாச பதி சூழ் கதிகள் மாறி may mean that even the soul's paths among bondage and the Lord fail in old age.

984.reading: Not knowing how to bow at the lotus feet the gods praise, the poet tells of embracing women within the net of their eyes on soft beds, asking 'is it honey, is it cane syrup, what equals it?', and asks whether he will not end the sorrow of countless unions and endless delusion. The praise names the anklets that went against Sura, the fierce peacock, Valli's bridegroom, the great one who told Siva the meaning of Veda and Agama without shyness, and Vishnu's nephew at Rameswaram.
984.nuance: The poet's question, தேனோ கருப்பில் எழு பாகோ இதற்கிணைகள் ஏதோ, is the lover's own praise of pleasure quoted against himself. ஞானபரற்கு இனிய வேதாகமப் பொருளை நாணாது உரைக்கும் பெரியோனே: the child teaching the father 'without shame', Murugan as guru to Siva.

links.note: Both show the man whose speech fails and who walks with a staff; the Naladiyar's old man still keeps his eyes on desire, while 983 traces the whole road from the price-women of youth to the staff and a catalogue of diseases.
